item.title: Touse or Bouse? How BU fraternities are ranked and mocked on Yik Yak
item.description: Boston University is home to 12 fraternities, many of which have begun the recruitment process for the spring 2026 semester by hosting “apartment crawls,” open houses and invite-only events. Following these recent functions, a wave of posts that rank, mock and criticize the campus fraternities emerged on Yik Yak, an app where college students post text and images anonymously among others in their campus community.

item.title: Stick Check: General managers in the hot seat
item.description: We’re 50 games and a goalie fight into the season, and NHL insiders and reporters are starting to buzz about trades and the postseason. Trade rumors and front office discussions have thrust general managers into the spotlight.

item.title: The cost of driving should be much higher | The MetroNome
item.description: New York City’s congestion pricing — already proven successful in cities like Stockholm and London — has forced those who drive through America’s most walkable city to subsidize their own private travel, rather than forcing other residents to foot the bill with lower air quality, more dangerous roads and lower-quality public transit.

item.title: Comfort and unease: the confusion of going home for winter break
item.description: Sometimes seeing this change makes me uncomfortable. For the month I was home, I caught myself feeling trapped and wanting to leave again, even though I had just arrived. Other times, it was soothing — I didn’t see home as a place that I wanted to escape from, but instead as a place, like college, that shaped me.

item.title: Payoff Pitch: The Hall of Fame has lost the plot
item.description: Two former baseball greats joined the ranks of the National Baseball Hall of Fame on Jan. 20, as the Baseball Writers’ Association of America’s 2026 balloting results were revealed on MLB Network.

item.title: From side hustle to main gig: Questrom graduate’s app aims to bring ease to on-campus services
item.description: Students across Boston University pay for all kinds of services. From manicures to spray tans to tutoring, some students spend hundreds of dollars a month to upkeep their physical appearances and lifestyles.
